items.followUp: State two differences between star topology and ring topology.

rubric.why: Identifies the shared cable used in a bus topology.
rubric.description: In a bus topology, all devices connect to a common backbone cable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the bus topology’s common backbone.

rubric.why: Identifies the direct device-to-device links in a full mesh.
rubric.description: In a full mesh, each device has a dedicated link to every other device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the connections in a full mesh.

rubric.why: Describes a consequence of failure of the shared bus cable.
rubric.description: Failure of the bus backbone can stop communication across the network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that backbone failure can disrupt the whole bus network.

rubric.why: Identifies the reliability advantage of mesh connections.
rubric.description: Mesh topology is reliable and fault tolerant because other links may remain available if one link fails.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying mesh topology’s reliability or fault tolerance.

modelAnswer: Bus topology: all devices are connected to one common backbone cable.
Mesh topology: in a full mesh, each device is connected to every other device by a dedicated link.
In bus topology, failure of the backbone can stop communication across the entire network.
Mesh topology is reliable and fault tolerant because other links may continue working if one link fails.

items.followUp: State two differences between RAM and a hard disk.

rubric.why: Describes the temporary nature of memory such as RAM.
rubric.description: Memory temporarily holds data and instructions currently in use and is usually volatile.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that memory is temporary or volatile.

rubric.why: Describes storage’s role in keeping data for continued use.
rubric.description: Storage keeps data and programs for long-term use and is generally non-volatile.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that storage retains data long-term or without power.

modelAnswer: Memory, such as RAM, temporarily holds data and instructions that the computer is currently using; it is usually volatile.
Storage keeps data and programs for long-term use and is generally non-volatile.

items.followUp: Draw the truth table for the AND operator.

rubric.why: Checks that both possible input values are included in the truth table.
rubric.description: Shows both input cases, 0 and 1, for A.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including both input values in the table.

rubric.why: Checks that each input has its correct inverted output.
rubric.description: Shows NOT A as 1 when A is 0 and as 0 when A is 1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both correct input-output pairings.
